name: tims-tandem
description: Silveira's second-generation TIMS tunnel with both funnels: 96 mm rather than 46, holding an ion accumulation trap upstream of the analysis region so that one population is accumulated while a previous one is mobility-analysed - the parallel-accumulation mode that gives a 100 per cent duty cycle. The storage region is a long rising edge, which is where the ion capacity the longer tunnel was built for comes from; the analysis region downstream of it is a shorter rising edge and a plateau ions elute across. The field on a rising edge goes as the square root of position, which the paper reports gives equivalent axial storage per mobility interval. The sequence is the published one: accumulate-and-elute at the same time, then a short transfer pulse that sweeps the stored population into the analysis region. This runs at the commercial operating point - 150 m/s of gas puts the parked ion near 47 townsend - so the declared low-field mobility is outside its fitted range and the run says so. It carries no space charge, which is what the extra electrodes exist for: the diffusive transport mode has no self-field, so this reproduces the timing benefit of two regions and not the capacity benefit.

ringCount.description: Rings in the 96 mm tunnel: 96 mm over the same 1.725 mm pitch.
ringCount.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 - a 96 mm tunnel, roughly twice the first generation's 46 mm

ringPitch.description: Board thickness plus the insulating gasket between plates.
ringPitch.source: Hernandez et al., Analyst 2014;139:1913 - 1.6 mm board, 0.125 mm kapton

boreRadius.description: Half the 8 mm tunnel bore, held constant along the analyser.

outerRadius.description: Outer edge of the ring boards. Not published; wide enough that the solve is insensitive to it.

tunnelLength.description: Derived from the ring count and pitch.

exitPotential.description: The potential the tunnel's profile reaches at its end: each region contributes its rising edge (one riseVolts) plus its plateau (1.5 riseVolts). Derived, so pulsing a region's field moves the end potential with it.

gasVelocity.description: Axial counterflow, from the pressure difference across the tunnel.
gasVelocity.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 - 3.1 and 0.9 mbar in the two funnel regions, giving ~150 m/s

gasPressure.description: Entrance-funnel-region pressure; the exit region is at 0.9 mbar and the gradient between them drives the flow. Declared as the reference rather than imported as a profile.

sourceX.description: Where the packet is released: in the funnel, well upstream of the gate, so it has to be delivered.

domainPad.description: Vacuum between the end elements and the solve's own grounded boundary. That boundary is a third electrode, and the end elements exist to keep it away from the bore.

detectorPad.description: Where the collecting plane sits past the tunnel exit.

exitLength.description: How far the exit element runs past the tunnel. The published exit funnel is 15 mm and this stands in for it at a single potential. Its length is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: a tube shields the bore over about one diameter, so anything shorter than the 8 mm bore lets the grounded domain boundary reach down the axis and reverse the field gradient before the tunnel even ends.
exitLength.source: Hernandez et al., Analyst 2014;139:1913 - exit funnel 15 mm

entranceLength.description: How far the entrance element runs before the tunnel. The published entrance funnel is 50 mm; this is a shorter stand-in at a single potential, long enough to shield the bore.

rfFrequency.description: Frequency of the quadrupolar RF on the ring segments.
rfFrequency.source: Ridgeway et al., IJMS 2018;425:22 - 850 kHz as the stated example; the 2011 prototype ran near 880 kHz

rfAmplitude.description: Zero-to-peak RF on each segment about its DC. Ridgeway's 200 Vpp is read as each segment swinging +-100 V with its neighbours in antiphase, so adjacent segments differ by 200 V zero to peak; the other reading - 200 Vpp between neighbours - is half this and a quarter of the well depth. Zero switches the confinement off.

rfQuadrupoleFraction.description: The quadrupole term four 90-degree segments at +-V produce on an 8 mm bore, relative to the hyperbolic ideal at the same electrode potential. 4/pi = 1.273 for segments meeting with no gap - a square wave's fundamental exceeds the square wave - less by what the gaps take.
rfQuadrupoleFraction.source: TimsRfCrossSectionStudy: the quadrupole coefficient of the solved four-segment cross-section with 0.5 mm gaps, sampled at half the bore radius

funnelLength.source: Hernandez et al., Analyst 2014;139:1913 - 50 mm entrance funnel

funnelPlateThickness.description: Funnel plate thickness, the same board as the tunnel rings.

funnelSpacing.source: Hernandez et al., Analyst 2014;139:1913 - 1.5 mm spacing in the funnels

funnelPlates.description: Plates in the funnel: 16 at the published length and pitch.

funnelEntranceRadius.description: Half the 26 mm bore at the funnel entrance; the funnel tapers linearly to the tunnel bore.
funnelEntranceRadius.source: Hernandez et al., Analyst 2014;139:1913 - 26 to 8 mm

funnelTaper.description: How much the inner radius shrinks per plate.

funnelOuterRadius.description: Outer edge of the funnel plates. Not published; wide enough that the solve is insensitive to it.

funnelRfAmplitude.description: Zero-to-peak RF on each funnel plate, adjacent plates in antiphase. Hernandez gives the phasing and not the amplitude; the tunnel's own 200 Vpp is taken as the funnel's too.

funnelDrop.description: DC dropped along the funnel from its entrance plate to its last plate, pushing positive ions toward the tunnel with the gas: 5 V/cm over 50 mm. Not published for this funnel; an ordinary funnel gradient.

gateThickness.description: The entrance gate electrode, a ring the same board as the rest.

gateGap.description: Gap either side of the gate.

gatePotential.description: The entrance gate: zero lets the funnel's ions through, raised holds what is in the tunnel and blocks what is not. Hernandez's sequence traces this as the entrance potential.

funnelStart.description: Distance from the tunnel entrance back to the funnel's first plate.

rfFringe.description: Over what distance the tunnel's quadrupolar RF rises from nothing at the tunnel entrance to full strength inside. A hard edge held 42 per cent of the delivered packet against the well; a real segmented ring's field decays over about a bore radius, and that is the value taken.

storageStart.description: Where the storage region's rising edge begins along the tunnel. The accumulation trap. Its rising edge takes most of the tunnel, which is where the capacity the longer tunnel was built for comes from - a mobility parks where the field balances the gas, so a longer edge spreads the same mobility range over more millimetres and more rings. The short plateau at the top is the barrier that holds everything parked behind it until the transfer pulse.
storageStart.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 fig. 1b - the storage and analysis bars, read off the figure

storageRise.description: Length of the storage region's rising edge, where ions park according to mobility.
storageRise.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 fig. 1b. The published 23 mm rise is cited for the first-generation 46 mm tunnel, not for this one

storagePlateau.description: Length of the storage region's plateau at peak field.
storagePlateau.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 fig. 1b. The published 18 mm plateau is the first generation's

storagePeakField.description: Axial field at the top of the storage region's rising edge, held across its plateau. Ridgeway reports up to ~70 V/cm across the tunnel; 50 V/cm holds every mobility whose v_g/K is below it. Lowering it is what releases: the analysis field is scanned and the storage field is pulsed.

storageRiseVolts.description: Potential gained across the rising edge. With the field going as the square root of position the potential goes as its three-halves power, so the integral is two thirds of the peak field times the length.

analysisStart.description: Where the analysis region's rising edge begins along the tunnel. The analysis region. A transferred population parks on its rising edge and elutes across its plateau as the field is scanned down. Shorter than the storage region because it holds one population at a time rather than accumulating.
analysisStart.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 fig. 1b - the storage and analysis bars, read off the figure

analysisRise.description: Length of the analysis region's rising edge, where ions park according to mobility.
analysisRise.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 fig. 1b. The published 23 mm rise is cited for the first-generation 46 mm tunnel, not for this one

analysisPlateau.description: Length of the analysis region's plateau at peak field.
analysisPlateau.source: Silveira et al., IJMS 2017;413:168 fig. 1b. The published 18 mm plateau is the first generation's

analysisPeakField.description: Axial field at the top of the analysis region's rising edge, held across its plateau. Ridgeway reports up to ~70 V/cm across the tunnel; 50 V/cm holds every mobility whose v_g/K is below it. Lowering it is what releases: the analysis field is scanned and the storage field is pulsed.

analysisRiseVolts.description: Potential gained across the rising edge. With the field going as the square root of position the potential goes as its three-halves power, so the integral is two thirds of the peak field times the length.

mobilityZeroField.description: The reference ion's low-field mobility, declared here as well as in transport so the field that balances the gas can be derived from it.
mobilityZeroField.source: Mason-Schamp from the cross section this template declares, at the declared pressure

balanceField.description: The field that holds the reference ion against the gas, v_g / K. Its parking point is where a rising edge reaches this value.

exitFunnelLength.description: Length of the exit funnel behind the tunnel.
exitFunnelLength.source: Hernandez et al., Analyst 2014;139:1913 - 50, 46 and 15 mm for entrance funnel, tunnel and exit funnel

exitFunnelExitRadius.description: Half the 1 mm bore where the exit funnel meets the next stage.
exitFunnelExitRadius.source: Hernandez et al., Analyst 2014;139:1913 - the exit funnel tapers 8 to 1 mm

exitFunnelPlates.description: Plates in the exit funnel, on the same board and spacing as the entrance funnel's: four at the published length and pitch.

exitFunnelTaper.description: How much the inner radius shrinks per exit-funnel plate.

exitFunnelDrop.description: DC dropped along the exit funnel, pulling eluted ions out of the tunnel toward the next stage. Not published; an ordinary funnel gradient.

exitFunnelRfAmplitude.description: Zero-to-peak RF on each exit-funnel plate, adjacent plates in antiphase, taken as the entrance funnel's. Hernandez gives the phasing and not the amplitude.

potential.expression: storageRiseVolts * (min(max((ring * ringPitch + ringThickness / 2) - storageStart, 0), storageRise) / storageRise) * sqrt((min(max((ring * ringPitch + ringThickness / 2) - storageStart, 0), storageRise) / storageRise)) + 1.5 * storageRiseVolts * min(max((ring * ringPitch + ringThickness / 2) - storageStart - storageRise, 0), storagePlateau) / storageRise + analysisRiseVolts * (min(max((ring * ringPitch + ringThickness / 2) - analysisStart, 0), analysisRise) / analysisRise) * sqrt((min(max((ring * ringPitch + ringThickness / 2) - analysisStart, 0), analysisRise) / analysisRise)) + 1.5 * analysisRiseVolts * min(max((ring * ringPitch + ringThickness / 2) - analysisStart - analysisRise, 0), analysisPlateau) / analysisRise
